newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Fujian executes 15 for kidnapping, murder.
newsitem.headline: China's Fujian executes 15 for kidnapping, murder.

text.p: Authorities in southeast China have executed 15 people for kidnapping, extortion and murder after the group was condemned during a mass sentencing attended by thousands, the Legal Daily said on Sunday.
The group was put to death on Saturday after the Fujian Higher People's Court slapped the death sentence on the kidnappers, the newspaper said.
More than 10,000 people, including officials of Changle and the provincial capital of Fuzhou, attended the mass sentencing in Changle city, it said.
Four co-defendants were given the death sentence suspended for two years, six others were sentenced to life imprisonment, and another 10 were given unspecified prison terms, it said.
The defendants were all farmers, the newspaper said. Their average age was 25, with the youngest 18.

They abducted several victims in Changle and the southern provinces of Guangdong and Jiangxi between December, 1995 and November, 1996 and extorted ransoms totalling 440,000 yuan ($53,000), the newspaper said.
They killed at least one of their victims, an 11-year-old student, it said without giving further details.
Crime, virtually eliminated in the years after the communists came to power in 1949, has resurfaced in the past two decades in the wake of economic reforms.

China frequently holds mass sentencing rallies at stadiums followed by executions of criminals in a bid to deter crime, triggering condemnation from international human rights groups. China has shrugged off the criticism as interference in its internal affairs.
